L6.1.quote: **Theorem A (proved):** for all $n$, $a_{n+1}$ = successor of $a_n$ in $S_\infty=\bigcap_m S_m$; hence the sequence is EXACTLY $S_\infty\cap[a_1,\infty)$.
L6.1.note: The characterization is stated, but no proof is included.

L6.2.note: Finiteness is explicitly identified as the remaining unproved crux; numerical evidence does not establish it.

L6.3.quote: So it suffices: $S_\infty$ is a union of residue classes mod $L$ (then $a_{n+T}=a_n+L$ for ALL $n$ with $T=\#(S_\infty\cap[1,L])$).
L6.3.note: The periodicity assembly is only conditional; finite-prime dependence and an actual valid L are not proved.

parsed.notes: The write-up gives a useful conditional framework, but supplies no written proof of characterization and expressly leaves the essential finiteness lemma open. Consequently global periodicity is not established.
